content:
Aiyana Brooks-Tan
Junior Frontend Developer
aiyana.brookstan@example.com | +353 55 555 0404
github.com/aiyana-bt-example | aiyana-bt.example.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Computing graduate and frontend developer with experience building React interfaces, improving web accessibility and writing unit tests. Full-stack project experience with TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL, including an accessible app using third-party weather and tide APIs.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS
Backend and databases: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL
Accessibility and testing: WCAG 2.1, screen-reader testing, Jest, React Testing Library
Tools: Git/GitHub, Storybook, Figma, Vercel

EXPERIENCE
Frontend Developer, Freelance | Oct 2025–Present
- Built a yoga studio booking website with Next.js and Tailwind CSS, including marketing pages, a class timetable and booking requests sent by email.
- Used static generation and deployed the site on Vercel; managed content in Markdown files.
- Made updates to two WordPress sites.

Teaching Assistant, First-Year Web Development Lab | Spring 2025
- Helped approximately 30 students during one semester of web development labs.

Software Development Intern, Harbourline Media | May 2024–Aug 2024
- Worked on the web team supporting the company's React news site.
- Fixed accessibility issues across more than 20 components, including keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels.
- Built a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages and documented it in Storybook.
- Wrote unit tests using Jest and React Testing Library.

Barista, Corner Bean Cafe | 2021–2025
- Worked part-time during studies.

PROJECTS
Tidewatch, Final-Year Project | 2024–2025
- Built an accessible web app showing tides, water temperature and weather for sea swimmers around the Irish coast.
- Developed a React and TypeScript frontend and a Node.js/Express API that cached data from public weather and tide APIs; used PostgreSQL for user favourites.
- Tested with NVDA and VoiceOver screen readers; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.
- Received 82% (First Class) and demonstrated the project at the college showcase.

Study Buddy, Group Project | 2023
- Built the React frontend and login screens for a study-session matching app in a team of four. Other team members developed the API and database.
- Used JavaScript and Firebase Authentication.

Student Hackathon | 2024
- Placed second in a team of three after building a transit delay notifier in 24 hours; developed the frontend.

EDUCATION
BSc (Hons) Computing – Software Development | Liffey Institute of Technology | 2021–2025
First Class Honours
Relevant modules: Web Development, Databases, Human-Computer Interaction, Software Testing, Data Structures & Algorithms

LANGUAGES
English: Native | Mandarin: Conversational

VOLUNTEERING
Manage social media for a sea swimming club.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, professional, well-structured junior developer CV. It presents relevant React, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL, accessibility, testing and Storybook experience prominently, and uses quantified evidence such as 20+ components, approximately 30 students and a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. The Tidewatch and yoga booking projects are especially relevant to a patient-facing booking product. The experience is truthful and appropriately distinguishes project experience from employment experience. The main content limitation is that some job-relevant areas—such as end-to-end testing, web security, semantic HTML and responsive design—are not evidenced, but these are candidate-experience gaps rather than writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional section headings, simple text formatting, standard employment and education structures, and relevant searchable keywords including React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, WCAG, Jest, React Testing Library, Git/GitHub, Next.js and Storybook. The inclusion of portfolio and GitHub links is helpful. AI screening probability is medium-high for junior frontend or junior full-stack searches, especially those prioritising accessibility and React, but lower for this specific vacancy because the document does not demonstrate two years of professional React/TypeScript experience, end-to-end testing, security fundamentals, or health-data privacy awareness. Do not add those keywords unless supported by actual experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with Verdane Care's technology and product context through React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Next.js, accessibility testing, Storybook, a booking website and a wellness-related yoga project. Tidewatch also supports alignment with the company's patient-first accessibility focus. Fluent English is shown, and the teaching-assistant experience supports the mentoring requirement at an early-career level. The candidate's material shows a gap against the requirement for 2+ years of professional React and TypeScript web-application experience: the CV shows a four-month internship and freelance work beginning in October 2025, while project experience is not professional employment. End-to-end testing, web security fundamentals, health-data privacy, German/Croatian, AWS or similar cloud platforms, Docker, and analytics/A/B testing are also gaps in the supplied candidate material. Semantic HTML and responsive layouts are not explicitly evidenced in the supplied material. The wellness experience is relevant, but there is no healthcare or regulated-environment experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary section, change the final sentence to make the project-based full-stack scope and testing evidence more specific without implying professional backend employment. For example: "Full-stack project experience with TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL, including Tidewatch, an accessible app using third-party weather and tide APIs, with Jest testing and screen-reader testing." The current wording is accurate, but this version better surfaces the testing keyword relevant to the role.
2. In the Projects section under Tidewatch, add the supported testing detail as a separate bullet: "Wrote Jest tests and tested the interface with NVDA and VoiceOver screen readers; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100." This uses information in the candidate portfolio and makes the project-level automated testing evidence easier for ATS and recruiters to find.
3. In the Skills section, change "Git/GitHub" to "Git and GitHub workflows" only if the candidate is comfortable describing their use this way. Otherwise retain the current wording. Do not add security, end-to-end testing, AWS, Docker, GDPR or health-data terms because they are not supported by the original candidate information.
4. In the Experience section, change the Teaching Assistant date from "Spring 2025" to "Spring 2025 (one semester)" and retain the bullet "Helped approximately 30 students during one semester of web development labs." This improves ATS date/context parsing and makes the mentoring evidence more immediately relevant.
5. In the Freelance experience heading, change "Frontend Developer, Freelance | Oct 2025–Present" to "Frontend Developer, Freelance (part-time) | Oct 2025–Present" if the work was part-time, as stated in the original candidate information. This preserves accuracy and prevents the role from being interpreted as full-time professional experience.
